findings.reason: the node must thread `path_prefixes` through every has-work predicate (triage, enrich, score, code, link), not just `has_pending_code_work`, or a scoped run stalls against facility-wide liveness checks.
findings.text: §14's code-claims node scopes the code claims but names only `has_pending_code_work` as the has-work predicate, while the orchestration wires FOUR facility-wide predicates into phase liveness: `has_pending_triage_work` (graph_ops.py:608, wired parallel.py:165), `has_pending_enrich_work` (graph_ops.py:623, wired parallel.py:169), `has_pending_score_work` (graph_ops.py:593, wired parallel.py:174) and `has_pending_code_work` (graph_ops.py:646, wired parallel.py:177), plus `has_pending_link_work` (graph_ops.py:670, wired parallel.py:181); the option's own help text (imas_codex/cli/discover/code.py:35–45) promises "the claim and its has-work predicate cover only the named trees", so as written the scoped `--path-prefix` run leaves that documented promise false for three phases and the phases never report done while any out-of-prefix file of theirs remains

findings.reason: the plan should express the bound through the existing `extra_filter` extension point (a spec default) or justify the new field, so the reset keeps one append mechanism.
findings.text: §14's stranded-row fix adds "a spec-level predicate that `reset_to_status` renders", but `reset_to_status` already accepts `extra_filter: str`/`extra_params` (reset.py:64–65) as its predicate-append extension point and renders them into the same WHERE clause (reset.py:94–98); the plan does not say whether the new bound reuses that mechanism or why a spec-owned field is required, risking a second predicate-append path beside the existing one

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §14 changes extend existing owners (one clause renderer, one create-nodes writer, one reset entry point) rather than spreading new shallow modules over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan scopes only one of the four facility-wide code has-work predicates, leaving the remaining three (and the link phase) as a parallel facility-wide owner of "work remaining" beside the scoped claims.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts are all 0; §14 is the only section adding surface (one renderer function plus parameters on `reset_to_status`, `create_nodes` and the code claims) and its own text names what it retires or merges (`seed_missing_roots` retired, `create_child_paths` deleted, the paths command's inline reset block replaced by the shared renderer), so the sections adding surface account for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §14 reuse map is accurate for the mechanisms it cites, but it proposes a new spec-level reset predicate without citing the existing `extra_filter`/`extra_params` append mechanism that `reset_to_status` already owns.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no new thin layer is added over an existing mechanism; `render_path_prefix_clause` is a consolidation of eight inline copies, not a wrapper, and the seed changes extend an existing call path.
